alt: Questions 1 (8 marks) and 2 (14 marks) are compulsory; candidates then choose two of Questions 3 to 5, worth 14 marks each. The paper lasts 1 hour 30 minutes and carries 50 marks, half the O Level.
caption: Two compulsory questions plus two from three: revise all four topics evenly.

alt: Two linked boxes: the Qur'an sets out core principles, and the Hadiths, a second source of guidance, give the practical detail of how they were lived out. A note defines Hadiths as the Prophet's sayings, actions and approvals, preserved through the isnad, distinct from the Qur'an but complementary.
caption: Principles from the Qur'an, practical detail from the Hadiths.

alt: Four numbered cards in succession: Abu Bakr, consolidating the community; Umar, expansion and administration; Uthman, standardising the Qur'an; and Ali, leadership during internal division. A bracket underneath says to compare them across the period.
caption: Know the order and one defining feature of each reign.

after: ## The Articles of Faith and Pillars of Islam
alt: The six Articles of Faith (Allah, angels, revealed books, prophets, the Day of Judgement and divine decree) lead to the five Pillars as the framework of practice: Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj. A warning reminds candidates to explain each, not just name it.
caption: Articles are what Muslims believe; Pillars are the practice built on them.

alt: A chain runs from the Prophet (pbuh) through narrators to the person recording the Hadith. Below, three steps: scholars checked each narrator's character and memory; so some Hadiths are classified as more reliable than others; and this scrutiny is why the Hadiths are treated as trustworthy.
caption: Mechanism, then result, then why it matters.

alt: Four mistakes with their fixes: listing the Articles or Pillars instead of explaining them; describing Caliphs in isolation instead of comparing them; treating Hadiths as equal to the Qur'an instead of complementary; and under-revising 2.4 instead of giving it equal rigour.
caption: Each common mistake has a simple fix: explain, compare, distinguish, revise evenly.
